# Validate the GPU metering data contract for chargeback reporting

## Description

Resolves the strategy's open question around the metering data schema. The
in-flight GPU usage metering strategy (RHAISTRAT-9990) owns the per-project
GPU-hour usage data schema, and that schema is not final until it lands. This
investigation validates the draft schema against chargeback reporting needs
and produces the consumption contract that all reporting work in this strategy
builds against, so that implementation can proceed against a stable interface
while the upstream schema finalizes. It also surfaces any schema gaps early
enough to be fed back to the metering strategy owners.

## Scope

- Review the metering strategy's draft data schema and its delivery path.
- Validate the draft schema against the reporting requirements:
  - per-project attribution of GPU-hour consumption
  - aggregation over selectable time ranges
  - the semantics of a GPU-hour (what counts as a GPU-hour)
- Define the reporting consumption contract: the data fields, semantics, and
  access path that reporting will build against.
- Identify gaps in the draft schema that would block or deform reporting, and
  communicate them to the metering strategy owners.
- Recommend whether reporting can proceed against the contract while the
  metering schema finalizes, and what adapter approach absorbs final-schema
  drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each reporting requirement (per-project attribution, time-range aggregation,
  GPU-hour semantics) is evaluated against the draft metering schema and marked
  supported or unsupported, with evidence.
- A consumption contract document exists specifying the data fields, semantics,
  and access path that reporting will build against.
- All schema gaps affecting reporting are documented and communicated to the
  metering strategy owners.
- A recorded recommendation states whether reporting can proceed against the
  contract before the metering schema finalizes, including the adapter approach
  for final-schema drift.

## HLR Traceability

De-risks HLR-1, HLR-2, and HLR-3 (all consume the metering data); resolves the
strategy's single open question, which gates the report implementation.

# Per-project GPU-hour reporting with CSV export and stable API

## Description

Delivers the core chargeback reporting capability: per-project GPU-hour
consumption reports over selectable time ranges, computed from the metering
data delivered by the GPU usage metering strategy, exportable as CSV and
retrievable via a stable API for finance tooling. Reporting builds against the
validated metering data consumption contract and absorbs final-schema drift
through an adapter, so the report API surface stays stable even if the
upstream metering schema changes before it finalizes.

## Scope

- Report computation: per-project GPU-hour totals over selectable time ranges,
  computed from metering data per the validated consumption contract.
- CSV export of reports.
- A stable, documented API for retrieving reports, suitable for finance
  tooling integration.
- An adapter layer that maps the consumption contract to the metering data as
  delivered, absorbing schema drift without changing the report API surface.
- Out of scope: the metering collection pipeline itself (owned by the GPU usage
  metering strategy) and currency/cost-rate modelling — reports are in
  GPU-hours, not dollars.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given metering data conforming to the consumption contract, per-project
  GPU-hour totals are computed correctly for selectable time ranges, verified
  against contract-conformant fixture data.
- Reports are exportable as CSV.
- Reports are retrievable via a documented, stable API suitable for finance
  tooling.
- Differences between the consumption contract and the final metering data
  schema are absorbed by the adapter without changing the report API surface.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time
  ranges.
- HLR-2 (P1): CSV export and stable API retrieval — shares the same report
  data structure and API surface as HLR-1, so it is bundled into this epic
  rather than split.

## Risks

- External timing: the metering data schema finalizes only when the GPU usage
  metering strategy (RHAISTRAT-9990) lands. This epic can be built and verified
  against contract-conformant data, but user-visible value requires the
  metering data to flow. The timing is externally controlled and cannot be
  compressed from this strategy.

# Dashboard admin view of current-month consumption against Kueue quota

## Description

Delivers the administrator-facing Dashboard view that shows each project's
current-month GPU-hour consumption against its Kueue quota. Quota figures come
from the platform's Kueue quota model; consumption figures come from the
per-project GPU-hour reporting capability. The Dashboard owns no data plane —
it presents data surfaced by the reporting API rather than computing reports
itself.

## Scope

- An administrator-facing view in the Dashboard console listing projects with
  their current-month GPU-hour consumption alongside their Kueue quota.
- Quota display based on the Kueue ClusterQueue/LocalQueue quota model.
- Consumption display fed by the GPU-hour reporting capability's API.
- Access gating consistent with existing Dashboard administrator views
  (OpenShift OAuth based RBAC).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Administrators can view per-project current-month GPU-hour consumption
  alongside each project's Kueue quota.
- Quota figures reflect the Kueue quota model (ClusterQueue/LocalQueue).
- The view is visible only to users with administrator access, consistent with
  Dashboard RBAC conventions.
- Consumption figures shown in the view match the GPU-hour reporting
  capability's output for the current month.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): the Dashboard admin view shows current-month consumption against
  each project's Kueue quota.

Delivers the user-facing documentation for GPU chargeback reporting: what the
reports mean (in particular, what counts as a GPU-hour) and how finance
tooling integrates with report export. The content is authored through the Red
Hat docs content process after the reporting and Dashboard capabilities are
implemented, so it describes what was actually built.

- Report semantics topic: what counts as a GPU-hour, how per-project
  attribution and time ranges work, consistent with the validated metering
  data consumption contract.
- Export integration topic: CSV export usage and the stable report API for
  finance tooling, including worked integration examples.
- Administrator-facing guidance for the Dashboard consumption-vs-quota view
  where it overlaps with report semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation defines report semantics, including the definition

  reporting capability.

- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented reporting and

Do not write the signals table into the epic body.\n211\t\n212\t## Step 6.5: Health Warnings\n213\t\n214\t### Non-blocking warnings (decomposition proceeds, human verifies later)\n215\t- Priority inversions (P0/P1/P2 inconsistent with technical complexity/reliability)\n216\t- Scope traps: ACs implying infrastructure that doesn't exist, contradictions between out-of-scope items and NFRs, storage beyond design intent\n217\t\n218\t### Handling unclear strategy passages\n219\t\n220\tWhen the strategy is unclear about something, apply this two-way distinction:\n221\t\n222\t| Situation | Handling |\n223\t|-----------|---------|\n224\t| **Implementation detail** — the team will resolve this when they start the work (version choices, API surface discovery, config decisions, validation of assumptions) | Not a flag. Do not set it earlier: anything you write or edit after setting it may be reviewed in a partially written state.\n351\t\n352\t### Conditional decomposition (when applicable)\n353\t\n354\tIf an Investigation epic has ≤3 bounded outcomes that change downstream structure, write one file per branch epic using the `-BRANCH-<letter>-` filename convention:\n355\t\n356\t```\n357\t{ID}-E001.md                        # Shared epic (the Investigation that selects the branch)\n358\t{ID}-BRANCH-A-E003.md               # If outcome A\n359\t{ID}-BRANCH-B-E003.md               # If outcome B\n360\t{ID}-BRANCH-B-E004.md               # Extra epic in branch B\n361\t```\n362\t\n363\t**Branch epics are not standalone Jira issues.** The pipeline attaches each branch's epics to the gating Investigation epic as a plan document; it does not create them as issues or wire Blocks links from them.
